From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Initial info request — DPF evidence and DPA annex

Michael — thanks for the note and the clear list. Attaching a consolidated evidence pack and a DPA annex draft. Quick summary up front:

- Processing locations: Hosted inference runs primarily in us-west-2 for your account by default; we can pin to us-east-1 or dedicated private deployments (VPC) on customer-owned subnets.
- Subprocessors: standard list included in the pack; we support subprocessor notifications and will provide a 30-day notice for new subprocessors with opt-out controls for enterprise contracts.
- Encryption: TLS 1.2+ in transit, AES-256 at rest. We support customer KMS (AWS KMS/HSM) for Private deployments and Dedicated with envelope encryption for Hosted; details in Key_Management_Controls_Summary.pdf.
- Logging & retention: token-level usage logs retained 90 days by default for hosted. Longer retention or export can be added under Dedicated/Private plans. Audit logs and signed attestations included.

Negotiable items: DPA annex routing language and retention windows are typically negotiable for enterprise contracts. Key-custody (customer-managed keys) is supported for Private deployments and can be extended to Dedicated with contractual terms.

Attachments: Redwood_DPF_Evidence_Pack_20280616.pdf, DPA_Annex_Draft_Aquilon_20280616.docx, Key_Management_Controls_Summary.pdf

I propose a 30-minute call Friday morning to walk through the pack and identify any sharp edges before your Monday meeting. When is good?

Thanks — Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Trust & Security | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
From: Sophie Lin <sophie.lin@aquilonhealth.com>

Karthik / Marissa — quick follow-up from our legal team: two specific clarifications they asked for after scanning the pack:

1) Cross-border routing: they want an explicit fallback sequence if the primary region is unavailable. Does Redwood support automated routing to a secondary region under SLA, and can we require the secondary be within the US or EU only?
2) Processor access: are there any cases where Redwood personnel would have access to plaintext customer data during troubleshooting for hosted customers? They want the conditions and approval path documented.

Also — can you confirm whether the encryption-at-rest supports customer key rotation without downtime?

Thanks,
Sophie
Sophie Lin
Sr. Counsel, Data Privacy | Aquilon Health
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Sophie Lin <sophie.lin@aquilonhealth.com>, Michael Jenkins <michael.jenkins@aquilonhealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-06-17T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial info request — DPF evidence and DPA annex

Hi Sophie — thanks for the detailed questions. Answering inline: 

1) Cross-border routing & fallback: our Smart Routing policy supports region-level routing with policy constraints. By default we route to the nearest healthy region and provide an ordered fallback list. For enterprise agreements we can lock the allowed fallback regions (e.g., restrict to US-only or EU-only) and include that as an annex to the DPA. Fallback is automated; we record event traces and will notify designated contacts when a cross-region failover occurs. Details are in the DPF pack (page 6).

2) Personnel access: for hosted customers, Redwood staff do not routinely access plaintext customer payloads. Support-level diagnostics capture telemetry and redacted request/response metadata. There are three narrow, auditable exceptions:
  - Emergency debugging of live incidents (requires two-person approval and logged ticket)
  - Customer-requested on-demand debug session (explicit written authorization and timebox)
  - Legal process (e.g., valid court order)
Each exception path is documented with required approvals and notification timelines; we can include a signed attestation if helpful.

3) Key rotation: for customer-managed KMS (Private or Dedicated with KMS integration) key rotation is supported without planned downtime using envelope keys and rolling re-encryption. We provide a runbook and recommend a maintenance window for large object rewraps; short-lived sessions and the runtime's envelope keys avoid cold starts. The Key_Management_Controls_Summary.pdf includes rotation timing and failure modes.

Next steps: we can mark the DPA annex with the US-only fallback clause you requested and prepare a one-page summary for your procurement meeting. Are you still available Friday for the call?

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Principal, Privacy & Compliance | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
